ezra: Filing a weird one - customer was throttled mid-stream after a truncate + reconnect. provisional_cost jumped and then dipped negative briefly.
tess: can you share the trace? sounds like the sampler/ledger ordering race again but curious about the truncate shapes.
ezra: clipped sequence: client streamed prefix P (credited), a toolcall truncated an in-flight suffix, reconnect resumed and the resumed stream emitted the truncated chunk (duplicate). sampler logged both; aggregator provisional sum went up, quota engine enforced, ledger later applied a dedupe adj and provisional became negative for a bit. customer saw a throttle and opened a ticket.
omar: paste logs if you have them.
ezra:```
[16:18:01.050] sample sess=ord-999 prefix=68 suffix=14 prov_tokens=82 price_hint=0.0005
[16:18:01.210] toolcall truncate suffix=14 tc_id=tc-77 credited_toolcall=true
[16:18:01.305] network reconnect resume-offset=68
[16:18:01.310] sample sess=ord-999 resumed_includes_truncated tokens=14 prov_tokens=14 price_hint=0.0005
[16:18:31.700] ledger commit sess=ord-999 confirmed_tokens=68 adjustment=-14 (dedupe tc-77)
```
tess: quota fired where? route or account?
ezra: route-level quota for /inference-batch - threshold small, provisional spike pushed it over.
chen: why negative provisional? provisional = sample_total - confirmed_total. When ledger applies a negative adjustment to confirmed_total (dedupe), confirmed_total goes down, so provisional can flip negative if sample_total had already decayed differently.
omar: small correction: dedupe adjustment reduces what would be double-billed in confirmed_total, usually lowering confirmed_total, so provisional might go up or down depending on sampling timing. negative provisional happens when confirmed_total is higher than latest sample_total due to reordering.
ezra: in this report provisional dipped to -12 tokens for ~7s then reconciled. customer saw a "you lost X provisional credits" message in console and panicked.
tess: ops asks: short-term UX mitigation: hide negative per-session provisional deltas in the console (show 0 and a tooltip) and prevent provisional-driven route-level enforcement from treating negative provisional as a refund signal.
omar: agree. For enforcement we should treat negative provisional as 0 (unless ledger emits an explicit refund event). That avoids turning a transient sampling artifact into an enforcement decision.
ops-bot: ALERT: billing-provisional-anomaly org=acme-sys sessions=[ord-999] flagged.
billing-bot: NOTE: final ledger confirmed charges are authoritative; provisional is best-effort.
ezra: engineering follow-up: add an aggregator-side monotonic sample_epoch per session and track "dedupe_marker" events from ledger so aggregator can immediately remove stale sample entries instead of waiting TTL. Also change quota engine to ignore provisional deltas originating from a different epoch until epoch stabilizes (5s).
chen: implementation sketch: aggregator keeps epoched buckets: tokens_by_epoch = {e1: 82, e2: 14}; when ledger dedupe arrives tagged with tc_id we immediately subtract corresponding entries from the epoch buffer and emit an "epoch_adjusted" event to the UI. Only after epoch_stable TTL do we roll epochs together for enforcement.
tess: short-term hotfix: clamp session_provisional_for_quota = max(0, min(raw_session_prov, session_threshold * 1.2)). low risk and prevents single-session spikes from instantly tripping route quotas. Add a console banner when clamp is applied.
omar: tests: unit tests for stream + truncate + reconnect + ledger dedupe flow, and an integration test that asserts quota not fired when ledger later dedupes. Also add an e2e sim that randomizes reconnect latency.
ezra: ops wants a CS blurb and a runbook entry for when customers see provisional dips vs refunds.
tess: I'll draft the CS blurb. ops-bot: created BI-20220 "CS message + runbook: provisional dips after reconnect/truncate" assigned @tess.
omar: I'll take ENG-6022 "Aggregator epoch buffers + dedupe markers". Plan: 1) sampler emits tc_id and sample_epoch on samples, 2) ledger emits dedupe_marker events for tc_id, 3) aggregator subtracts immediately and marks epoch_adjusted, 4) quota_engine ignores pre-epoch tokens until stable TTL.
ezra: thanks. please make the UI clamp a quick patch so CS can show customer a calm dashboard screenshot. :thumbsup:
